title: Heterogeneous computing: choosing resources under communication, power, and numerical constraints
status: reviewed and locally validated; independent round 2 ACCEPT
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions; no verified audio review

frame_inspection_methods.detail: Contact sheets use 800 × 450 selected frames. Quantitative, code and architectural terminology claims were also inspected in original 1280 × 720 frames where relevant. Frame 75 f0036 contains credits and supplies no material claim.

source_uncertainties: No audio verification was performed. Machine-transcript discrepancies are not attributed as spoken errors.

PUE/linear-power/exponential-communication wording appears in the machine transcript; the inspected PUE-era frame only has qualitative power/cooling bullets. Public text gives supported definitions and constructed countermodels, without alleging those exact spoken/slide errors.

Grace Hopper and Dojo frames list examples but do not establish same-die or in-vehicle claims. The chapter uses NVIDIA 2022 chip-to-chip documentation and Tesla April 2026 training/inference distinction.
Current availability/performance of the lecture-era processor, packaging, cloud and memory examples is not audited or implied. No deadline for the end of Moore-style scaling is established.
Dennard 1974 and Bekenstein 1981 were relied upon only at their publicly opened abstract scope. The ideal scaling algebra is an original model, not a claimed full-paper reproduction.
The CUDA guide identifies itself as legacy; used for stable block-barrier semantics. Runtime web documentation13.4 is separate from the installed CUDA 13.3.73 captured locally.
No quantum, neuromorphic, optical, FPGA, ASIC, simultaneous CPU/GPU partition, multi-GPU, inter-node or physical-energy experiment was performed.
CPU sweeps include a maximum-change reduction absent from the GPU sweep kernel. Fixed-sweep payloads match, but this is not a comparison of identical convergence-checking work.

references.title: MPI 4.1 nonblocking communication
references.supports: Initiation/completion separation; overlap permitted but not required
